FRBRname.value: Ordonnance du 18 mai 2005 sur la réduction des risques liés à l'utilisation de substances, de préparations et d'objets particulièrement dangereux (Ordonnance sur la réduction des risques liés aux produits chimiques, ORRChim)
Ordinance of 18 May 2005 on the Reduction of Risks relating to the Use of Certain Particularly Dangerous Substances, Preparations and Articles (Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance, ORRChem)

Ordinanza del 18 maggio 2005 concernente la riduzione dei rischi nell'utilizzazione di determinate sostanze, preparati e oggetti particolarmente pericolosi (Ordinanza sulla riduzione dei rischi inerenti ai prodotti chimici, ORRPChim)
Verordnung vom 18. Mai 2005 zur Reduktion von Risiken beim Umgang mit bestimmten besonders gefährlichen Stoffen, Zubereitungen und Gegenständen (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV)

preface.p: English is not an official language of the Swiss Confederation. This translation is provided for information purposes only and has no legal force.

p.docTitle:
Ordinance
on the Reduction of Risks relating to the Use of Certain Particularly Dangerous Substances, Preparations and Articles

preamble.p:
on the basis of Articles 2 paragraph 4, 19, 22 paragraph 2, 24, 38, 39 paragraph 2,
44 paragraph 2, 45 paragraphs 2 and 5 and 46 paragraph 1 of the Chemicals Act of 15 December 2000
SR 813.1 (ChemA),
on the basis of Articles 27 paragraph 2, 29, 30a, 30b, 30c paragraph 3, 30d, 32abis,
38 paragraph 3, 39 paragraphs 1 and 1bis, 41 paragraph 3, 44 paragraphs 2 and 3,
46 paragraphs 2 and 3, 48 paragraph 2 and 63 paragraph 2 of the Environmental Protection Act of 7 October 1983
SR 814.01 (EPA),
on the basis of Articles 9 paragraph 2 letter c, 27 paragraph 2 and 48 paragraph 2 of the Federal Act of 24 January 1991
SR 814.20 on the Protection of Waters,
on the basis of Article 15 paragraphs 4 and 5 of the Foodstuffs Act of 20 June 2014
SR 817.0 ,
and of Article 56 paragraph 2 of the Energy Act of 30 September 2016
SR 730.0 (EnA), and in implementation of the Federal Act of 6 October 1995
SR 946.51 on Technical Barriers to Trade,
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance:

item.p: prohibits or restricts the use of the particularly dangerous substances, preparations and articles covered by the Annexes;
specifies the personal and professional qualifications required for the use of certain particularly dangerous substances, preparations and articles.

blockList.listIntroduction: Without prejudice to specific disposal requirements laid down in this Ordinance, substances, preparations and articles which are waste, as defined in Article 7 paragraph 6 EPA, are subject to:

item.num:
a.
Amended by Annex 6 No 11 of the Waste Management Ordinance of 4 Dec. 2015, in force since 1 Jan. 2016 (AS 2015 5699).

b.
Amended by Annex 3 No II 8 of the O of 22 June 2005 on Movements of Waste, in force since 1 Jan. 2006 (AS 2005 4199).
item.p:
the Ordinance of 22 June 2005
SR 814.610 on Movements of Waste; and

the Ordinance of 14 January 1998
SR 814.620 on the Return, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment.

blockList.listIntroduction: This Ordinance does not apply to:

item.p: the transport of substances, preparations and articles by road, rail, water, air or pipelines;

item.num:
b.
Amended by Annex 4 No 45 of the Customs Ordinance of 1 Nov. 2006, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1469).
item.p: the transit of substances, preparations and articles under customs supervision, provided that they do not undergo any processing or transformation.

blockList.listIntroduction:
In this Ordinance, without prejudice to specific definitions given in the Annexes:
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Dec. 2012 (AS 2012 6161).

item.p: manufacturer means any natural or legal person who manufactures, extracts or imports substances, preparations or articles on a professional or commercial basis; also deemed to be a manufacturer is any person who obtains substances, preparations or articles in Switzerland and supplies them on a professional or commercial basis, without altering their composition, under his own trade name or for some other purpose; if a person arranges for the manufacture of a substance, preparation or article in Switzerland by a third party, this person is deemed to be the sole manufacturer if he is domiciled or has a registered office in Switzerland;
trader means any natural or legal person who obtains substances, preparations or articles in Switzerland and supplies them on a commercial basis without altering their composition.

chapter.heading: Use of Substances, Preparations and Articles

content.p: The restrictions and prohibitions on the use of specific substances, preparations and articles, together with exemptions, are regulated in the Annexes.
Exemptions under the Annexes are only granted to persons who are domiciled or have a registered office in Switzerland.

section.num:
Section 1a
Inserted by Annex No 2 of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).
section.heading: Special Labelling

content.p: Special labelling must be clearly legible and indelible. It must be in at least one official language of the place where the substance, preparation, appliance or article is supplied to users or the where the system is installed.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following may be labelled in different official language or in English with the agreement of the individual professional users:

item.p: a substance or preparation for supply to professional users;
appliances and systems for professional users.

content.p: The official languages are German, French and Italian.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I 6 of the O of 4 Sept. 2013 (Reorganisation in the field of Food Safety and Veterinary Medicine), in force since 1 Jan. 2014 (AS 2013 3041).

content.p: The following applications require an authorisation granted by the authorities mentioned below:

item.p: application, on a professional or commercial basis, of products intended to protect plants against rodents (rodenticides), if applied on more than one farm or by machine

td.p: cantonal authority; with the agreement of the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO), the Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG) and the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) in the case of regional or supra-regional applications

item.num:
b.
Amended by Annex 10 No II 5 of the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 20 Aug. 2025, in force since 1 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 565).
item.p: aerial spraying and spreading of plant protection products, basic substances, biocidal products and fertilisers

td.p: Federal Office of Civil Aviation, with the agreement of the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH), the FSVO, the FOAG, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and the FOEN

item.num:
c.
Amended by Annex 10 No II 5 of the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 20 Aug. 2025, in force since 1 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 565). Correction of 23 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 864).
item.p: application of biocidal products, plant protection products, basic substances and fertilisers in forests, unless covered by an authorisation under letter a or b

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

article.heading: Applications that do not require authorisation

content.p: The granting of authorisation in accordance with Article 4 letter b is not required for the application of organisms using an unmanned aircraft.

Authorisation shall be granted in accordance with Article 4 letter a or c if the planned application is not expected to endanger the environment. This authorisation is for a limited period and for a specific geographical area.
Amended by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

blockList.listIntroduction: Authorisation granted in accordance with Article 4 letter b shall be limited in time and geographical scope and only granted if, in the case of the planned application:

item.p: application from the ground is not feasible or application from the air is associated with advantages for the protection of human health or the environment;
the aviation company uses aircraft and equipment with state-of-the-art technology for the protection of human health and the environment; and

there is no reason to fear any risk to human health and the environment.
Inserted by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

content.p: Authorisations shall only be granted to persons who are domiciled or have a registered office in Switzerland or in a member state of the European Union (EU) or the European Free Trade Association (EFTA).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

content.p: If a federal authority is responsible for the authorisation, it shall consult the relevant cantonal authority before making a decision, in particular in relation to whether the cantonal authority takes the view that the conditions for authorisation have been fulfilled and regarding the ancillary requirements to be stipulated in any authorisation that may be granted. The federal authority shall notify the cantonal authority of its decision.

article.heading: Use of substances and preparations requiring a certificate

blockList.listIntroduction: The following activities may only be carried out on a professional or commercial basis by natural persons with an appropriate certificate or with a qualification regarded as equivalent, or acting under the supervision of such persons:
the use of:

item.p: plant protection products,
pesticides on behalf of third parties,
disinfectants for use in public swimming pools,
wood preservatives;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Dec. 2012 (AS 2012 6161).

blockList.listIntroduction: the handling of refrigerants during:

item.p: the manufacture, installation, maintenance or disposal of refrigeration, air conditioning or heat recovery appliances or systems,
the disposal of refrigerants.

content.p: Pest control with fumigants may only be carried out by natural persons with an appropriate certificate or with a qualification regarded as equivalent.

The competent Federal Department shall specify detailed requirements for certificates. It may provide for exemptions to authorisation requirements. It shall take account of the protection goals.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

blockList.listIntroduction: A certificate shall be issued to a person who, in an examination, has demonstrated the knowledge required for the activity concerned with regard to:

item.p: fundamentals of ecology and toxicology;
legislation on the protection of the environment, health and workers;
measures for the protection of the environment and health;
environmental impacts and the appropriate use and disposal of substances, preparations and articles;
appliances and their appropriate handling.

content.p:
Certificates from member states of the EU and EFTA are regarded as equivalent to Swiss certificates; the provisions on certificates for the use of plant protection products are reserved.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

The competent Federal Department or its designated agency shall decide, if requested by a college or vocational training establishment, whether a specific qualification must be regarded as equivalent to a certificate. Such equivalence does not apply to the use of plant protection products.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

The competent Federal Department shall determine which agency may recognise occupational experience as equivalent to a certificate and under what conditions. Such equivalence does not apply to the use of plant protection products.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

blockList.listIntroduction: Articles 9–11 apply mutatis mutandis to:

item.p: certificates from member states of the EU and EFTA (para. 2);
qualifications regarded as equivalent to a certificate (para. 3);
occupational experience recognised as equivalent to a certificate (para. 4).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

article.heading: Certificates for the use of plant protection products issued by member states of the EU and EFTA

content.p:
Equivalence in accordance with Article 8 paragraph 2 does not apply to certificates for the use of plant protection products whose holder is established in Switzerland within the meaning of the Agreement of 21 June 1999
SR 0.142.112.681 between the Swiss Confederation, of the one part, and the European Community and its Member States, of the other, on the free movement of persons or Annex K of the Convention of 4 January 1960
SR 0.632.31 establishing the European Free Trade Association.

At the request of the holder of a relevant certificate from a member state of the EU or EFTA, the competent Federal Department shall decide on the recognition of the requesting person’s professional qualifications. Recognition shall make it possible for a Swiss certificate to be granted.

If the competent Federal Department finds significant differences between the foreign and the related Swiss qualification, it shall offer measures to compensate for these differences (compensation measures), in particular in the form of an examination or an adaptation course.
Recognition is not required for service providers. However, they must comply with the Swiss law on reporting requirement and the review of professional qualifications.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

article.heading: Geographical scope and period of validity

content.p: Certificates are valid throughout Switzerland.

The certificate permitting the professional or commercial use of plant protection products in accordance with Article 7 paragraph 1 letter a is valid for five years. It shall be extended for a further five years, provided that the holder has completed the continuing education and training in accordance with Article 10 before the expiry of the certificate's period of validity.
The competent Federal Department may restrict the period of validity of certificates.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

content.p: Any person who holds a certificate and carries out the relevant activities must keep abreast of best practices and undergo continuing education and training.

If necessary, the competent Federal Department may regulate the details of the mandatory continuing education and training, in particular with regard to its scope, content and conditions, as well as the recognition and monitoring of institutions for continuing education and training.

In the case of certificates permitting the professional or commercial use of plant protection products, the continuing education and training must be completed at an institution for continuing education and training recognised by the FOEN.

blockList.listIntroduction:
If the holder of a certificate wilfully infringes the relevant provisions of environmental, health and worker protection legislation, or repeatedly infringes such provisions through negligence, the cantonal authority may, by means of a ruling:
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

item.p: require the person concerned to attend a course or take an examination; or
temporarily or permanently revoke the certificate.

content.p: The cantonal authority shall inform the competent Federal Office of such rulings.
The Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC) is responsible for certificates as specified in Article 7 paragraph 1 letter a numbers 1 and 4, and letter b.
The Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) is responsible for certificates as specified in Article 7 paragraph 1 letter a numbers 2 and 3, and paragraph 2.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Department shall define:

item.p: the content, scope and procedure for examinations;
the documentation requirements for examining bodies.

content.p:
The Department or its designated agency shall specify the examining bodies that conduct examinations and issue certificates. The certificates permitting the professional and commercial use of plant protection products shall be issued by the FOEN.
Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).
DETEC shall provide opportunities for preparation for examinations within its sphere of responsibility.

blockList.listIntroduction: In the case of certificates permitting the professional and commercial use of plant protection products:

item.p: the FOEN shall decide in response to a written request whether an institution for continuing education and training may be recognised for offering a continuing education and training course within the meaning of Article 10;
the FOEN shall monitor the institutions for continuing education and training;

the FOEN shall revoke its recognition of an institution for continuing education and training if it fails to implement any corrective measures ordered despite being warned beforehand.
Inserted by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

article.heading: Funding of examining bodies and institutions for continuing education and training

blockList.listIntroduction: Based on Article 49 paragraph 1 EPA and in response to an application made to the FOEN, the Confederation may grant financial assistance for basic and continuing education and training. The bodies and institutions may claim financial assistance for education and training in the following fields:

item.p: agriculture;
horticulture;

specialist fields, in particular the use of herbicides in agriculture and in the maintenance of railway and military installations and the maintenance of the grounds of residential, service, commercial, industrial and public buildings;
forestry.

content.p: Financial assistance shall be provided in the form of flat-rate payments amounting to a maximum of 50 per cent of the costs of efficient education and training. This includes the planning, organisation, preparation and conduct of examinations and basic and continuing education and training courses.

DETEC shall decide on the content and objectives of the basic and continuing education and training and shall stipulate the criteria for granting financial assistance in an ordinance. The content, objectives and criteria shall in principle apply for the period to which the funding decision relates.
In the absence of regulations to the contrary, the cantons are responsible for monitoring compliance with the provisions of this Ordinance.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Confederation is responsible for:

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Dec. 2012 (AS 2012 6161).
item.p: the tasks assigned to it in Articles 4, 7–12 (certificates) and 19;
the granting of authorisations in accordance with the Annexes;
enforcement of the provisions concerning imports and exports;
enforcement with regard to substances, preparations and articles serving the interests of national defence.

article.heading: Delegation of tasks and powers to third parties

content.p: The competent federal agencies may delegate to appropriate public bodies or private individuals some or all of the tasks and powers assigned to them by this Ordinance.
Insofar as the enforcement of health protection is concerned, delegation is limited to Articles 7–12 (certificates) and the provision of information under Article 28 of the Chemicals Act.

With regard to medical devices, enforcement is based on the Medical Devices Ordinance of 17 October 2001
SR 812.213 .

With regard to substances, preparations and articles relating to systems and activities serving the interests of national defence, Article 82 of the Chemicals Ordinance of 5 June 2015
SR 813.11 (ChemO) applies.
Amended by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

With regard to fertilisers, the enforcement provisions of the Fertiliser Ordinance of 1 November 2023
SR 916.171 also apply.
Amended by Annex 5 No II 3 of the Fertilisers Ordinance of 1 Nov. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 711).

At the request of the FOPH, FOAG or FOEN, customs offices shall check whether substances, preparations and articles comply with the provisions of this Ordinance.
Amended by Annex 4 No 45 of the Customs Ordinance of 1 Nov. 2006, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1469).

In cases of suspected infringement, they are authorised to detain goods at the border and call in the other enforcement authorities in accordance with this Ordinance. These authorities shall carry out further investigations and take the necessary measures.

On a spot-check basis or at the request of the FOPH, FOAG, FOEN or SECO, the cantonal enforcement authorities shall inspect substances, preparations and articles placed on the market at the premises of manufacturers, traders and professional or commercial users. They shall check whether the substances, preparations and articles comply with the provisions of the Annexes, in particular with regard to composition, labelling and information for purchasers.
Amended by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).
They shall also check whether the use of these substances, preparations and articles complies with the requirements of this Ordinance.

If the substances, preparations or articles inspected or the use thereof give cause for complaint, the inspection authority shall inform the authorities responsible for rulings under Article 19. If the latter are cantonal authorities, it shall additionally inform the FOPH, FOEN and SECO and also, in cases of complaints concerning plant protection products, the FSVO and the FOAG, and in cases of complaints concerning fertilisers, the FOAG.
Amended by Annex 10 No II 5 of the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 20 Aug. 2025, in force since 1 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 565).

If an inspection reveals that provisions of this Ordinance have been violated, the federal authority or the authority of the canton in which the manufacturer, trader or user is domiciled or has a registered office shall, by means of a ruling, order the necessary measures.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 10 No II 5 of the Plant Protection Products Ordinance of 20 Aug. 2025, in force since 1 Dec. 2025 (AS 2025 565).

article.heading: Specialist advice on the use of fertilisers, plant protection products and basic substances

content.p: The cantons shall ensure that specialist advice is offered on the use of fertilisers, plant protection products and basic substances, and that funding is available for these services.

blockList.listIntroduction: They may require persons who use fertilisers, plant protection products and basic substances on a professional or commercial basis in polluted areas:

item.p: to avail themselves of the specialist advice offered for this purpose;
to make available the operational data required for such advice.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 1 July 2015, in force since 1 Sept. 2015 (AS 2015 2367).

content.p:
Data confidentiality and the exchange of data among enforcement authorities and with other countries are governed by Articles 73–76 of the ChemO
SR 813.11 .

The obligation to pay fees and the calculation of fees for administrative acts performed by the federal enforcement authorities in accordance with this Ordinance are based on the Chemicals Fees Ordinance of 18 May 2005
SR 813.153.1 .
The transitional provisions on certificates in accordance with Articles 7–12 shall be enacted by the competent Federal Department.

Exemptions granted under the Substances Ordinance of 9 June 1986
[AS 1986 1254; 1988 911; 1989 270, 2420; 1991 1981; 1992 1749; 1994 678; 1995 1491 Art. 440 No 2, 4425 Annex 1 No II 14, 5505; 1997 697; 1998 2009, 2863 Annex 5 No 3; 1999 39, 1362, 2045 Annex 2 No 3; 2000 703 No II 9, 1949 Art. 22 para. 2; 2001 522 Annex No 2, 1758, 3294 No II 6; 2003 940, 1345, 5421 No II 2; 2004 3209, 4037 No I 7. AS 2005 2695 No I 1]. remain valid for the period originally specified.
Applications for exemptions which are pending when this Ordinance comes into force shall be assessed according to this Ordinance.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex No 2 of the O of 11 March 2022 (AS 2022 220). Amended by No I of the O of 16 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2022 788).

article.heading: Transitional provisions to the Amendment of 16 November 2022

content.p: Holders of a licence to use plant protection products that was granted in accordance with the provisions of the former Article 8 paragraphs 1, 3 or 4 that were valid until 31 December 2025 may apply to the FOEN by 30 June 2026 for the licence to be replaced.

Where an application has been submitted in respect of licences granted under the previous law by 30 June 2026, the licences shall be replaced by a certificate valid for five years, which shall be recorded in the Register of PPP Certificates in accordance with Article 1 of the Ordinance of 16 November 2022
SR 814.88 on the Register of Certificates for the Use of Plant Protection Products.
Holders of a licence acquired before 1 January 2000 must successfully complete all the continuing education and training courses required in accordance with Article 9 paragraph 3 by 31 December 2029.
Licences granted under the previous law expire on 1 January 2027.
This Ordinance comes into force on 1 August 2005.

container.block:
Annex 1.1
Amended by No II para. 1 of the O of 1 July 2015 (AS 2015 2367). Revised by No I of the O of 25 Oct. 2017 (AS 2017 5963), of 17 April 2019 (AS 2019 1495), of 23 Feb. 2022 (AS 2022 162), No I para. 3 of the O of 29 Oct. 2025, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2025 747) and the correction of 16 July 2026 (AS 2026 394).

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 It is prohibited to manufacture, place on the market, import on a private basis or use:

item.p: persistent organic substances as specified in Number 3;
substances and preparations containing persistent organic substances as specified in Number 3 which are not merely unavoidable impurities.

content.p: 2 New articles may not be placed on the market if they or their components contain persistent organic substances as specified in Number 3 which are not merely unavoidable impurities.

blockList.listIntroduction: 3 Annex 1.16 applies to the following substances:

item.p: perfluorooctane sulfonic acid and its derivatives (PFOS);
perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS) and its precursor compounds;
perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and its precursor compounds.

content.p: 4 For electrical and electronic equipment that contains hexabromobiphenyl or brominated diphenyl ethers, Annex 2.18 applies.
5 For decabromodiphenyl ether, Annex 1.9 numbers 2 and 4 apply.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 do not apply to:

item.p: manufacture, placing on the market and use for analysis and research purposes;
lubricating oils and greases manufactured from waste oils if the content of persistent organic substances does not exceed 0.0001 % by mass (1mg/kg).

blockList.listIntroduction: 1bis The prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 letter b do not apply to substances and preparations, provided that:

item.p: their content of alkanes C10–C13, chloro- does not exceed 1 % by mass;
their content of brominated diphenyl ethers as specified in Number 3 letter d does not exceed 0.001 % by mass (10 mg/kg).

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The prohibition specified in Number 1 paragraph 2 do not apply to articles and their components, provided that:

item.p: their content of alkanes C10–C13, chloro does not exceed 0.15 % by mass;
their content of tetra-, penta-, hexa- and heptabromodiphenyl ether as specified in Number 3 letter d does not exceed 0.001% by mass (10mg/kg).

content.p: 3 In addition, the prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 letter b and paragraph 2 do not apply to preparations and articles manufactured partially or fully from recycled materials or materials from waste prepared for re-use, provided that their content of tetra-, penta-, hexa- and heptabromodiphenyl ether as specified in Number 3 letter d does not exceed 0.1 % by mass.

level.heading: List of prohibited persistent organic pollutants

item.p: Hexachlorobutadine (CAS no 87-68-3);
Alkanes C10–C13, chloro (CAS no 85535-84-8);
Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid and its derivatives (PFOS);
Hexachlorocyclohexane (HCH, all isomers);
Hexabromocyclododecane (HBCDD, isomers of CAS no 25637-99-4, CAS no 3194-55-6, CAS no 134237-50-6, CAS no 134237-51-7 and CAS no 134237-52-8);

cyclo[12.2.1.16,9.02,13.05,10]octadeca-7,15-diene (Dechlorane Plus, CAS No. 13560-89-9) including its anti- and syn-isomers (CAS No. 135821-74-8 and CAS No. 135821-03-3).
Pentachlorobenzene (CAS no 608-93-5);

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to:
the placing on the market of the following articles containing Dechlorane Plus that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030:

item.p: articles with applications in the aerospace and defence industry,
devices for medical imaging,
devices and equipment for radiotherapy,
components for the manufacture of articles, equipment and installations in accordance with items 1-3;

blockList.listIntroduction: the placing on the market of spare parts containing Dechlorane Plus for the repair of the following articles until 31 December 2043, if Dechlorane Plus was used in the manufacture of these articles:

item.p: motor vehicles that were first placed on the market before 1 January 2026,
stationary machinery for agriculture, forestry and construction that was first placed on the market before 1 January 2026,
devices with applications in shipping, forestry and gardening that were first placed on the market before 1 January 2026,
analysis, measuring, control, monitoring, testing, production and inspection equipment, including in vitro diagnostic medical devices, which were first placed on the market before 1 January 2026,
articles with applications in the aerospace and defence industry that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030,
medical imaging devices that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030,
devices and systems for radiotherapy that were placed on the market for the first time before 26 February 2030;
the placing on the market of all other articles containing Dechlorane Plus that were first placed on the market in Switzerland or an EU or EFTA Member State before 1 January 2026;

blockList.listIntroduction: the placing on the market and use of Dechlorane Plus and preparations containing Dechlorane Plus for:

item.p: the manufacture of articles, devices, systems and components in accordance with letter a until 25 February 2030,
the manufacture of spare parts that may be placed on the market in accordance with letter b.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The prohibition specified in Number 1 paragraph 2 does not apply to:
the placing on the market of the following articles containing UV-328 that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030:

item.p: motor vehicles and their components,
aircraft and their spare parts, each containing UV-328 in tapes, adhesives or coatings,
railway vehicles, production machinery and large steel structures that each contain UV-328 in coatings,
mechanical separators in blood collection tubes,
triacetylcellulose film in polarisers and articles containing such polarisers,
photo paper;

blockList.listIntroduction: the placing on the market of spare parts containing UV-328 for the repair of the following articles until 31 December 2043 if UV-328 was used in the manufacture of these articles:

item.p: stationary machinery for agriculture, forestry and construction that was first placed on the market before 1 January 2026,
motor vehicles that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030;
liquid crystal displays in analysis, measurement, control, monitoring, testing, production and inspection equipment placed on the market for the first time before 26 February 2030,
liquid crystal displays in medical devices that were first placed on the market before 26 February 2030;
the placing on the market of all other articles containing UV-328 that were first placed on the market in Switzerland or an EU or EFTA Member State before 1 January 2026.

blockList.listIntroduction: 3 The FOEN may, in response to a justified application, grant temporary exemptions from the prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 for the placing on the market and use of preparations containing UV-328 and UV-328 for:

item.p: the manufacture of articles specified in paragraph 2 letter a: until 25 February 2030;
the manufacture of spare parts that may be placed on the market in accordance with paragraph 2 letter b: until 31 December 2043.

content.p: 4 The FOEN shall grant an exemption in accordance with paragraph 3 if the measures required to protect human health and the environment are taken and emissions of UV-328 into the environment are reduced to a minimum.

blockList.listIntroduction: 5 An application in accordance with paragraph 3 must contain at least the following information:

item.p: the location of the use;
the intended use of UV-328 or preparations containing this substance;
the expected quantities used and information on the expected environmental impact of UV-328;
a description of the measures taken to minimise environmental inputs of UV-328 and human exposure as far as technically feasible and economically viable.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 It is prohibited to manufacture, place on the market, import on a private basis or use:

item.p: halogenated organic substances as specified in Number 3;
substances and preparations containing halogenated organic substances as specified in Number 3 which are not merely unavoidable impurities.

content.p: 2 It is prohibited to place new textiles and new leather goods on the market if they or their components contain substances as specified in Number 3 letters a – e which are not merely unavoidable impurities.
3 It is prohibited to place on the market new articles if they or their components contain substances as specified in Number 3 Letters f and g which are not merely unavoidable impurities.
4 For chlorinated biphenyls and naphthalenes and hexabromobiphenyl, Annex 1.1 applies.
5 For electrical and electronic equipment that contain octabromodiphenyl ether, Annex 2.18 applies.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 do not apply to:

item.p: manufacture, placing on the market and use for analysis and research purposes;

mono- and di-halogenated biphenyls, terphenyls and naphthalenes and to preparations that contain such substances if they are used exclusively as intermediate products in synthesis and are merely contained in finished products as unavoidable impurities;
lubricating oils and greases manufactured from waste oils if their content of halogenated biphenyls does not exceed 0.0001 % (1mg/kg) by mass;
the manufacture of 1,2,4 trichlorobenzene and substances and preparations containing 1,2,4 trichlorobenzene;

blockList.listIntroduction: the placing on the market and use of 1,2,4 trichlorobenzene and of substances and preparations containing 1,2,4 trichlorobenzene as:

item.p: intermediate products in synthesis, in particular for the manufacture of 1,3,5-trinitro-2,4,6-triaminobenzene,
process solvents in closed systems in chlorination reactions;
the placing on the market and use of substances and preparations with a maximum concentration of 0.1 % 1,2,4 trichlorobenzene by mass.

content.p: 2 The prohibition specified in Number 1 paragraph 2 does not apply to the import of new textiles and new leather goods which are only finished or repackaged in Switzerland and then re-exported in their entirety.

3 In relation to the substance specified in Number 3 letter g, the prohibition specified in Number 1 paragraph 3 does not apply to the placing on the market of articles if their content of octabromodiphenyl ether does not exceed 0.1 % by mass.

telodrin (CAS no 297-78-9).

perthane (CAS no 72-56-0).

pentachlorophenoxy compounds;

monomethyl-tetrachloro-diphenyl methane (CAS no 76253-60-6);
monomethyl-dichloro-diphenyl methane;

2-(2,4,5-Trichlorphenoxy) propionic acid (CAS no 93-72-1) and its salts, and 2-(2,4,5-trichlorophenoxy) propionyl compounds.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 It is prohibited to place on the market or use the following substances:

item.p: chloroform (CAS no 67-66-3);
1,1,2-trichloroethane (CAS no 79-00-5);
1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane (CAS no 79-34-5);

content.p: 2 It is also prohibited to place on the market or use substances and preparations containing 0.1% or more, by mass, of the substances specified in paragraph 1.
3 It is prohibited to use hexachloroethane (CAS no 67-72-1) in the manufacturing or processing of non-ferrous metals.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to:

item.p: medicinal products;
substances and preparations intended for use in closed systems in industrial processes;
substances and preparations intended for analysis and research.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 On receipt of a justified request, the FOEN may, with the agreement of the SECO and the FOPH, grant temporary exemptions from the prohibitions specified in Number 1 paragraphs 1 and 2 for the use of chloroform if:

item.p: according to the state of the art, no substitute for chloroform is available for the use in question; and
the quantity of chloroform used is no greater than is required for the intended purpose and does not exceed 20 litres per year.

content.p: 1 The packaging of substances and preparations specified in Number 2 letter c must be marked as follows: «For industrial use only».

Verordnung vom 18. Mai 2005 zur Reduktion von Risiken beim Umgang mit bestimmten besonders gefährlichen Stoffen, Zubereitungen und Gegenständen (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV)

level.heading: Substances that deplete the ozone layer

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 Substances that deplete the ozone layer are:
all fully halogenated chlorofluorocarbons with up to three carbon atoms (CFCs), such as:

item.p: trichlorofluoromethane (CFC 11),
dichlorodifluoromethane (CFC 12),
tetrachlorodifluoroethane (CFC 112),
trichlorotrifluoroethane (CFC 113),
dichlorotetrafluoroethane (CFC 114),
chloropentafluoroethane (CFC 115);

blockList.listIntroduction: all hydrochlorofluorocarbons with up to three carbon atoms (HCFCs), such as:

item.p: chlorodifluoromethane (HCFC 22),
dichlorotrifluoroethane (HCFC 123),
dichlorofluoroethane (HCFC 141),
chlorodifluoroethane (HCFC 142);

blockList.listIntroduction: all fully halogenated bromofluorocarbons with up to three carbon atoms (halons), such as:

item.p: bromochlorodifluoromethane (halon 1211),
bromotrifluoromethane (halon 1301),
dibromotetrafluoroethane (halon 2402);
all partially halogenated hydrobromofluorocarbons with up to three carbon atoms (HBFCs);
1,1,1-trichloroethane (CAS no 71-55-6);
carbon tetrachloride (CAS no 56-23-5);
bromomethane (CAS no 74-83-9);
bromochloromethane (CAS no 74-97-5).

content.p: 2 Preparations containing substances specified in paragraph 1 are deemed equivalent to substances that deplete the ozone layer if they are found in containers used solely for the transport or storage of these preparations.
3 Regenerated substances that deplete the ozone layer are substances produced by re-processing of used ozone depleting substances without chemical modification.
It is prohibited to manufacture substances that deplete the ozone layer.
The prohibition specified in Number 2.1 does not apply to the manufacture of regenerated substances that deplete the ozone layer.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 It is prohibited to place on the market preparations and articles which:

item.p: contain substances that deplete the ozone layer;

were manufactured with substances that deplete the ozone layer and are listed in an Annex to the Montreal Protocol of 16 September 1987
SR 0.814.021 on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer (Montreal Protocol).

blockList.listIntroduction:
2 Substances that are listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2024/573
Regulation (EU) 2024/573 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 7 February 2024 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, amending Directive (EU) 2019/1937 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 517/2014, version as per OJ L, 2024/573, 20.2.2024. and are ozone-depleting substances must be placed on the market in reusable containers if they are intended for use:

item.p: in accordance with Annex 2.9 number 3.3; or
in systems or equipment that may be placed on the market or imported for private purposes in accordance with Annex 2.10 numbers 2.1 and 2.2 and Annex 2.11 numbers 2.1 and 2.2.

blockList.listIntroduction: The prohibition specified in Number 3.1 does not apply to the placing on the market of:

item.p: preparations and articles for whose manufacture or maintenance substances that deplete the ozone layer may be used in accordance with Number 6.2 or on the basis of an exemption granted under Number 6.3.1 paragraph 1;

preparations and articles which may be placed on the market in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.9–2.11 and which, if imported, are imported from countries that comply with the provisions of the Montreal Protocol and the Amendments to the Protocol of 29 June 1990
SR 0.814.021.1 , 25 November 1992
SR 0.814.021.2 , 17 September 1997
SR 0.814.021.3 and 3 December 1999
SR 0.814.021.4 , as approved by Switzerland
The list of these states can be found in the said amendments to the Montreal Protocol (SR 0.814.021.1/.4) in the section ‘Scope of application on …’. ;
preparations deemed equivalent to substances that deplete the ozone layer as specified in Number 1 paragraph 2.

content.p: Any person wishing to import substances that deplete the ozone layer as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1, or who intends to store such substances in an open customs warehouse, in a warehouse for bulk goods or in a duty-free warehouse, requires an import licence from the FOEN.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 An import licence is granted on application, provided that:

item.p: the substances that deplete the ozone layer which are intended to be imported are for a permitted use as specified in Number 6.2 or the intended user has been granted an exemption in accordance with Number 6.3.1 paragraph 1; and

the import comes from countries that have approved the Montreal Protocol and its amendments of 29 June 1990, 25 November 1992, 17 September 1997 and 3 December 1999
The list of these states can be found in the said amendments to the Montreal Protocol (SR 0.814.021.1/.4) in the section ‘Scope of application on …’. .

content.p: 2 In addition, for substances specified in Number 1 paragraph 1, the import licence is only issued for the quantities and uses approved by the Parties to the Montreal Protocol.
1 The import licence is granted in the form of a general import licence.
2 A general import licence entitles the holder to import specific quantities of substances that deplete the ozone layer from specific foreign exporters. It is personal and non-transferable.

3 The FOEN shall inform the cantons and the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS)
The name of this administrative unit was changed on 1 Jan. 2022 pursuant to Art. 20 para. 2 of the Publications Ordinance of 7 Oct. 2015 (SR 170.512.1) (AS 2021 589). This change has been made throughout the text. of the granting and revocation of general import licences.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The application must include:

item.p: the applicant’s name and address;
the names and addresses of the foreign exporters;

blockList.listIntroduction: for each substance to be imported, the following information:

item.p: the chemical name according to an internationally recognised nomenclature,

the customs tariff number according to the Annexes of the Federal Act of 9 October 1986
SR 632.10 on Customs Tariffs (CTA),
the intended quantity, expressed in kilograms per calendar year,
the intended uses.

content.p: 2 The FOEN may request further information on the origin and intended use of the substances concerned.
1 The FOEN shall make a decision on the complete application within two months.
2 A general import licence is issued for a maximum period of 18 months; it expires at the end of a calendar year and is numbered.

level.heading: Obligations relating to import and storage

content.p:
1 The person required to submit a declaration under Article 26 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005
SR 631.0 (CustA) must specify the number of the general import licence in the customs declaration.
2 At the request of the customs office, the person required to submit a declaration must submit a copy of the import licence as specified in Number 3.3.5 paragraph 1.
3 On storage in an open customs warehouse, in a warehouse for bulk goods or in a duty-free warehouse, the storer or depositor must enter the number of the import licence in an inventory record.
It is prohibited to export articles the use of which requires substances that deplete the ozone layer as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 letters a, c–f and h.

blockList.listIntroduction: For substances that deplete the ozone layer as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 with a gross mass of more than 20kg, an export licence from the FOEN is required by any person wishing to:

item.p: export such substances; or
move such substances to another country from an open customs warehouse, a warehouse for bulk goods or a duty-free warehouse.

content.p:
An export licence shall be granted on application if the export is to countries that have approved the Montreal Protocol and its amendments of 29 June 1990, 25 November 1992, 17 September 1997 and 3 December 1999
The list of these states can be found in the said amendments to the Montreal Protocol (SR 0.814.021.1/.4) in the section ‘Scope of application on …’. .
1 The export licence is granted in the form of a specific export licence.

2 An export licence entitles the holder to export, on one occasion, specific quantities of substances that deplete the ozone layer to a specific foreign importer in a country that complies with the Montreal Protocol provisions approved by Switzerland. It is personal and non-transferable.
3 The FOEN shall inform the cantons and the FOCBS of the granting and revocation of export licences.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The application must include:

item.p: the applicant’s name and address;
the name and address of the foreign importer;

blockList.listIntroduction: for each substance to be exported, the following information:

item.p: the chemical name according to an internationally recognised nomenclature,
the customs tariff number according to the Annexes of the CTA,
the name and address of the previous owner,
the intended quantity, expressed in kilograms.

content.p: 2 The FOEN may request further information on the origin and intended use of the substances concerned.
1 The FOEN shall make a decision on the complete application within two months.
2 An export licence shall be issued for a maximum period of 12 months and shall be numbered.

level.heading: Obligations relating to export and removal from storage

content.p: 1 The person required to submit a declaration under Article 26 CustA must specify the number of the export licence in the customs declaration.
2 The person required to submit a declaration must submit a copy of the export licence with the customs declaration.
3 On removal from an open customs warehouse, a warehouse for bulk goods or a duty-free warehouse, the storer or depositor must enter the number of the export licence in an inventory record.

level.heading: Reporting requirements for imports and exports

content.p: 1 Any person who imports or exports substances that deplete the ozone layer as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 or preparations as specified in Number 1 paragraph 2 must inform the FOEN each year by 31 March of the quantities imported or exported during the previous year.
2 The reports must be classified by substance and intended use.

The reporting requirements specified in Number 5.1 paragraph 1 do not apply to storage in, or removal to another country from, a customs bonded warehouse, a bulk goods warehouse or a duty-free warehouse.
It is prohibited to use substances that deplete the ozone layer.

1 The prohibition specified in Number 6.1 does not apply to the use of substances that deplete the ozone layer for the manufacture of preparations or articles which may be placed on the market or imported for private purposes in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.9–2.11.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 If, according to the state of the art, no substitute is available for the substances that deplete the ozone layer or for the preparations and articles manufactured using these substances, the prohibition specified in Number 6.1 does not apply to the use of substances that deplete the ozone layer:

item.p: as intermediate products for complete subsequent chemical conversion;

for the laboratory or analytical purposes permitted in accordance with Decision X/19 of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol
The text of this Decision may be obtained at www.ozone.unep.org > Treaties > Montreal Protocol > Decisions of the Meetings of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol > Twenty-Sixth Meeting of the Parties > Decision XXVI/5. .

content.p: 1 On receipt of a justified application, the FOEN may grant temporary exemptions for other uses of substances that deplete the ozone layer.
2 It shall inform the cantons of the granting and revocation of exemptions.

blockList.listIntroduction: An exemption may be granted if:

item.p: according to the state of the art, no substitute is available for the substances that deplete the ozone layer or for the preparations and articles manufactured using these substances; and
the quantity of substances that deplete the ozone layer being used is no greater than is required for the intended purpose.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 An application must include:

item.p: the applicant's name and address;
the chemical name of the substance according to an internationally recognised nomenclature;
the safety data sheet for the substance;
the name and address of the supplier of the substance;
information about the intended use, including the quantities to be used and disposed of per year;
the intended disposal method;
a description of the measures to prevent or reduce emissions of the substance concerned throughout its lifetime;
a description of the research and development activities undertaken to avoid the use of the substance concerned.

content.p: 2 The FOEN may request further information on the substance concerned and its intended use.
3 Applications under Number 6.3.3 paragraph 1 must be submitted at least 14 months before the start of the calendar year in which the use is to take place.

The FOEN shall decide on complete applications within two months of receiving the decision of the Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol on the quantity of a particular substance which may be used during a particular period.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The manufacturer may only place on the market containers that contain or will contain substances listed in Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2024/573 and that are ozone-depleting substances if their labelling contains the following information:

item.p: the text: "Contains fluorinated greenhouse gases";
the abbreviated chemical names of the substances contained or to be contained in the containers, using the industrial nomenclature accepted for the area concerned;
the quantity of substances, in kg and tonnes of CO2 equivalents, and the global warming potential of the substances.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The manufacturer of containers that contain or will contain substances referred to in paragraph 1 in recycled or reclaimed form in accordance with Article 3 paragraphs 12 and 13 of Regulation (EU) 2024/573 or in regenerated form in accordance with Number 1 paragraph 3 must indicate this on the containers:

item.p: the quality of the fabrics;
the name and address of the facility where the substances have been recycled, reprocessed or regenerated.

content.p: Preparations and articles which were manufactured with substances that deplete the ozone layer and are listed in an Annex to the Montreal Protocol (No. 3.2.1 let. b) may continue to be imported for one year after the relevant Annex to the Montreal Protocol comes into force.

Verordnung vom 18. Mai 2005 zur Reduktion von Risiken beim Umgang mit bestimmten besonders gefährlichen Stoffen, Zubereitungen und Gegenständen (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV)

container.block:
Annex 1.5
Amended by No I of the O of 17 April 2019 (AS 2019 1495). Revised by the Annex to the O of 24 Nov. 2021 (AS 2021 859), No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022 (AS 2022 162), Annex No 2 of the O of 11 March 2022 (AS 2022 220) and No I para. 3 of the O of 29 Oct. 2025, in force since 1 Jan. 2026 (AS 2025 747).

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 Substances stable in the atmosphere are:

item.p:
other fluorinated organic compounds
The list of the most common other fluorinated organic compounds may be obtained at www.bafu.admin.ch > Chemikalien > Fachinformationen > Bestimmungen and Verfahren > in der Luft stabile Stoffe. with a vapour pressure of at least 0.1 mbar at 20ºC or whose boiling point does not exceed 240ºC at 1013.25 mbar, and which have a mean atmospheric lifetime of at least 2 years;
sulfur hexafluoride (CAS no 2551-62-4);
nitrogen trifluoride (CAS no 7783-54-2).

blockList.listIntroduction: 1bis For the purposes of the obligation in accordance with Number 9 paragraph 2, nitrous oxide (CAS no 10024-97-2) also applies as a substance stable in the atmosphere, provided the nitrous oxide is generated as a by-product in the manufacture of the following substances:

item.p: nitric acid (CAS no 7697-37-2);
caprolactam (CAS no 105-60-2);
adipic acid (CAS no 124-04-9);
glyoxal (CAS no 107-22-2) and glyoxylic acid;
nicotinic acid (CAS no 59-67-6);

substances other than those named in letters a–e that are generated from a reaction with nitrous oxides or nitric acid, provided nitrous oxide is generated in a comparable volume to that in the manufacture of the substances named in letters a–e.

content.p: 2 Preparations containing substances specified in paragraph 1 are deemed equivalent to substances stable in the atmosphere if they are found in containers used solely for the transport or storage of these preparations.
3 Regenerated substances stable in the atmosphere are substances produced by reprocessing of used substances stable in the atmosphere without chemical modification.

level.heading: Substances stable in the atmosphere which are substances that deplete the ozone layer

content.p: For substances stable in the atmosphere which are substances that deplete the ozone layer, Annex 1.4 applies.
The manufacture of hydrofluorocarbons as specified in Number 1 letter a is prohibited.
The prohibition specified in Number 3.1 does not apply to the manufacture of regenerated hydrofluorocarbons.
1 It is prohibited to place on the market preparations and articles containing substances stable in the atmosphere.

blockList.listIntroduction:
2 Substances that are listed in one of Annexes I-III of Regulation (EU) 2024/573
Regulation (EU) 2024/573 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 7 February 2024 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, amending Directive (EU) 2019/1937 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 517/2014, last amended by OJ L, 2024/573, 20.2.2024. and are stable in the atmosphere must be placed on the market in reusable containers if they are intended for use:

item.p: in accordance with Annex 2.3 number 4.2 or Annex 2.9 number 3.3; or

in systems or devices that may be placed on the market or imported for private purposes in accordance with Annex 2.10 numbers. 2.1 and 2.2, Annex 2.11 numbers 2.1 and 2.2 and Annex 2.19 numbers 2.1 and 2.2.

blockList.listIntroduction: Without prejudice to Number 8 paragraph 1, the prohibition specified in Number 4.1 paragraph 1 does not apply to the placing on the market of:

item.p: preparations and articles for whose manufacture or maintenance substances stable in the atmosphere may be used in accordance with Number 6.2 or on the basis of an exemption granted under Number 6.3.1 paragraph 1;

preparations and articles that may be placed on the market in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.3 and 2.9-2.11 and articles that may be placed on the market in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.12 and 2.19; and
preparations deemed equivalent to substances stable in the atmosphere as specified in Number 1 paragraph 2.

content.p: Any person wishing to import hydrofluorocarbons as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 letter a, or who intends to store them in an open customs warehouse, in a warehouse for bulk goods or in a duty-free warehouse, requires an import licence from the FOEN.

Without prejudice to Number 8 paragraph 1, an import licence is granted on application, provided that the hydrofluorocarbons which are intended to be imported are for a permitted use as specified in Number 6.2 or the intended user has been granted an exemption in accordance with Number 6.3.1 paragraph 1.
1 The import licence is granted in the form of a general import licence.
2 A general import licence entitles the holder to import specific quantities of hydrofluorocarbons from specific foreign exporters. It is personal and non-transferable.
3 The FOEN shall inform the cantons and the FOCBS of the granting and revocation of general import licences.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 An application must include:

item.p: the applicant's name and address;
the names and addresses of the foreign exporters;

blockList.listIntroduction: for each substance to be imported, the following information:

item.p: the chemical name according to an internationally recognised nomenclature,

the customs tariff number according to the Annexes of the Customs Tariff Act of 9 October 1986
SR 632.10 (CTA),
the intended quantity, expressed in kilograms per calendar year,
its quality (new, used, regenerated),
the intended uses.

content.p: 2 The FOEN may request further information on the origin and intended use of the substances concerned.
1 The FOEN shall make a decision on the complete application within two months.
2 A general import licence is issued for a maximum period of 18 months; it expires at the end of a calendar year and is numbered.

level.heading: Obligations relating to import and storage

content.p:
1 The person required to submit a declaration under Article 26 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005
SR 631.0 (CustA) must specify the number of the general import licence in the customs declaration.
2 At the request of the customs office, the person required to submit a declaration must submit a copy of the import licence.
3 On storage in an open customs warehouse, in a warehouse for bulk goods or in a duty-free warehouse, the storer or depositor must enter the number of the import licence in an inventory record.

blockList.listIntroduction: For hydrofluorocarbons as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 letter a with a gross mass of more than 20kg, an export licence from the FOEN is required by any person wishing to:

item.p: export such substances; or
move such substances to another country from an open customs warehouse, a warehouse for bulk goods or a duty-free warehouse.

content.p: An export licence is issued if the applicant submits a complete application as specified in Number 5.4.
1 The export licence is granted in the form of a specific export licence.
2 A specific export licence entitles the holder to export, on one occasion, specific quantities of hydrofluorocarbons. It is personal and non-transferable.
3 The FOEN shall inform the cantons and the FOCBS of the granting and revocation of export licences.

blockList.listIntroduction: An application must include:

item.p: the applicant's name and address;
the name and address of the foreign importer;

blockList.listIntroduction: for each substance to be exported, the following information:

item.p: the chemical name according to an internationally recognised nomenclature,
the customs tariff number according to the Annexes of the CTA,
the name and address of the previous owner,
the intended quantity, expressed in kilograms, broken down by calendar year, importer and recipient country,
its quality (new, used, regenerated).

content.p: 1 The FOEN shall make a decision on the complete application within two months.
2 An export licence is issued for a period of 12 months and is numbered.

level.heading: Obligations relating to export and removal from storage

content.p: 1 The person required to submit a declaration under Article 26 CustA must specify the number of the export licence in the customs declaration.
2 The person required to submit a declaration must submit a copy of the export licence with the customs declaration.
3 On removal from an open customs warehouse, a warehouse for bulk goods or a duty-free warehouse, the storer or depositor must enter the number of the export licence in an inventory record.
It is prohibited to use substances stable in the atmosphere.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 Without prejudice to paragraph 2, the prohibition specified in Number 4.1 does not apply to the use of substances stable in the atmosphere:

item.p: for the manufacture or maintenance of preparations or articles that may be placed on the market or imported for private purposes in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.3 and 2.9-2.11, as well as articles that may be placed on the market or imported for private purposes in accordance with the provisions of Annexes 2.12 and 2.19;
5% of the quantity of substances used;
as an intermediate in a process leading to complete chemical conversion, provided that emissions do not exceed 0.5% of the quantity of substances used;
as heat transfer or insulation fluids in welding machines and in testing and calibration baths;
as medicinal products or medical devices;
for research and analysis purposes.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The exceptions under paragraph 1 only apply if:

item.p: no state-of-the-art alternative is available either for the substances stable in the atmosphere or for the preparations and articles manufactured with or containing these substances;
the quantity and the global warming potential of the substances stable in the atmosphere being used are no greater than is required for the intended purpose according to the state of the art; and
emissions of substances stable in the atmosphere are kept as low as possible throughout the life cycle of the intended use.

content.p: 3 After consulting the industry concerned and the cantonal authorities responsible for enforcing this Ordinance, the FOEN shall issue recommendations on the state of the art in accordance with paragraph 2.
1 On receipt of a justified request, the FOEN may grant temporary exemptions for other uses of substances stable in the atmosphere.
2 It shall inform the cantons of the granting and revocation of exemption permits.

blockList.listIntroduction: An exemption may be granted if:

item.p: according to the state of the art, no substitute is available either for the substances stable in the atmosphere or for the preparations and articles manufactured with these substances;
the quantity and the global warming potential of the substances stable in the atmosphere being used is no greater than is required for the intended purpose according to the state of the art; and
emissions of substances stable in the atmosphere are kept as low as possible throughout the life cycle of the intended use.

blockList.listIntroduction: An application must include:

item.p: the applicant's name and address;
the chemical name of the substance according to an internationally recognised nomenclature;
the safety data sheet for the substance;
the name and address of the supplier of the substance;
information about the intended use, including the quantities to be used and disposed of per year;
the intended disposal method;
a description of the measures to prevent or reduce emissions of the substance concerned throughout its lifetime;
a description of the research and development activities undertaken to avoid the use of the substance concerned.

level.heading: Reporting requirements for importers and exporters

content.p: 1 Any person who imports or exports substances stable in the atmosphere as specified in Number 1 paragraph 1 or preparations as specified in Number 1 paragraph 2 must inform the FOEN each year, by 31 March, of the quantities imported or exported during the previous year.
2 The reports must be classified by substance and intended use.

blockList.listIntroduction: The reporting requirements specified in Number 7.1.1 paragraph 1 do not apply to:

item.p: storage in, or removal to another country from, an open customs warehouse, a warehouse for bulk goods or a duty-free warehouse;
importers and exporters who are party to a sectoral agreement, as defined in Article 41a of the Environmental Protection Act, if this agreement ensures that the FOEN will be duly informed.

level.heading: Reporting requirements for appliances and systems containing sulfur hexafluoride

content.p: 1 Any person commissioning or decommissioning an appliance or system containing more than 1kg sulfur hexafluoride must inform the FOEN accordingly.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 The report must contain the following data:

item.p: the type and location of the appliance or system;
the quantity of sulfur hexafluoride contained therein;
the date of commissioning or decommissioning;
in the case of decommissioning: the recipient of the sulfur hexafluoride..

content.p: 1 Parties to a sectoral agreement, as defined in Art. 41a of the Environmental Protection Act, on sulfur hexafluoride are exempt from the reporting requirements specified in Number 7.2.1 paragraph 1 if this agreement ensures that the FOEN will be duly informed.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 Reporting is not required for:

item.p:
appliances or systems containing more than 1kg sulfur hexafluoride in hermetically sealed pressure systems in accordance with SN EN 62271-1:2008
This standard may be viewed free of charge at or obtained for a fee from the Schweizerische Normenvereinigung (SNV), Sulzerallee 70, 8404 Winterthur; www.snv.ch . if one party to a sectoral agreement assumes responsibility for reporting.
appliances or systems serving the interests of national defence.

content.p: The FOEN is responsible for reporting of data in accordance with Article 7 paragraph 3 of the Montreal Protocol.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The manufacturer may only place on the market containers that contain or will contain substances that are listed in one of Annexes I-III of Regulation (EU) 2024/573 and are stable in the atmosphere if their labelling contains the following information:

item.p: the text: «Contains fluorinated greenhouse gases»;
the abbreviated chemical names of the substances contained or to be contained in the containers, using the industrial nomenclature accepted for the area concerned;
the quantity of substances, in kg and tonnes of CO2-equivalents, and the global warming potential of the substances.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1bis The manufacturer of containers that contain or will contain substances mentioned in paragraph 1 in recycled or reclaimed form in terms of Article 3 paragraphs 12 and 13 of Regulation (EU) 2024/573 or in regenerated form in terms of Number 1 paragraph 3 must indicate on the containers:

item.p: the form of the substances;
the name and address of the facility in which the substances were recycled, reclaimed or regenerated.

content.p: 2 The manufacturer of devices or systems containing more than 1 kg of sulphur hexafluoride must indicate this substance on the devices or systems and state the quantity of this substance contained in the devices or systems. For electrical systems and electrical devices containing sulphur hexafluoride as an insulating gas, the labelling requirements according to Annex 2.19 Number 2.3 apply.

level.heading: Obligations in relation to chemical conversion processes

content.p: 1 Any person who initiates chemical conversion processes in which substances stable in the atmosphere in accordance with Number 1 paragraph 1 may be generated as a by-product shall ensure that no more than 0.5% of the quantity of starting material used is emitted as these substances.

2 Any person who manufactures substances in accordance with Number 1 paragraph 1bis must convert the nitrous oxide generated as a by-product in accordance with the state of the art provided this is technically and operationally feasible and economically viable.

level.heading: Monitoring the conversion of nitrous oxide from manufacturing processes

content.p: 1 The FOEN shall monitor compliance with the obligation in accordance with Number 9 paragraph 2.

2 If the monitoring indicates that the obligation is not being complied with, the FOEN shall take the measures required. If necessary, it shall order the discontinuation of the manufacturing process concerned.

1 If an alternative is available for substances stable in the atmosphere that were authorised for use on the basis of Number 6.2 paragraph 1 letter b-f in conjunction with paragraph 2 due to a change in the state of the art, these substances may continue to be used for the purposes specified in these letters for a period of 12 months.

2 …
Comes into force on 1 Jan. 2028 (AS 2025 747).

FRBRname.value: Ordonnance du 18 mai 2005 sur la réduction des risques liés à l'utilisation de substances, de préparations et d'objets particulièrement dangereux (Ordonnance sur la réduction des risques liés aux produits chimiques, ORRChim)
Ordinance of 18 May 2005 on the Reduction of Risks relating to the Use of Certain Particularly Dangerous Substances, Preparations and Articles (Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance, ORRChem)

Ordinanza del 18 maggio 2005 concernente la riduzione dei rischi nell'utilizzazione di determinate sostanze, preparati e oggetti particolarmente pericolosi (Ordinanza sulla riduzione dei rischi inerenti ai prodotti chimici, ORRPChim)
Verordnung vom 18. Mai 2005 zur Reduktion von Risiken beim Umgang mit bestimmten besonders gefährlichen Stoffen, Zubereitungen und Gegenständen (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV)

container.name: headerOfAnnex
container.block:
Annex 1.6
Revised by No I of the O of 17 April 2019 (AS 2019 1495), of 23 Feb. 2022 (AS 2022 162) and Annex No 2 of the O of 11 March 2022, in force since 1 May 2022 (AS 2022 220).

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 Asbestos refers to the natural fibrous silicate minerals of:

item.p: actinolite (CAS no 77536-66-4);
amosite (CAS no 12172-73-5);
anthophyllite (CAS no 77536-67-5);
chrysotile (CAS no 12001-29-5);
crocidolite (CAS no 12001-28-4);
tremolite (CAS no 77536-68-6).

content.p: 2 Asbestos-containing preparations are preparations in which asbestos is present not merely as an unavoidable impurity.

3 Asbestos-containing articles are articles in which asbestos is present not merely as an unavoidable impurity, and appliances and equipment such as vehicles, machines or instruments with asbestos-containing components.

blockList.listIntroduction: It is prohibited:

item.p: to use asbestos;
to place asbestos-containing preparations or articles on the market;
to export asbestos-containing preparations or articles;
to use asbestos-containing preparations or articles.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 On receipt of a justified request and with the agreement of the FOPH, the FOEN may grant exemptions to the prohibitions specified in Number 2 letters a and b if:

item.p: according to the state of the art, no substitute for asbestos is available and the quantity of asbestos used is no greater than is required for the intended purpose;
on account of particular design characteristics, only asbestos-containing spare parts can be used; or
on aesthetic grounds, no asbestos-free substitute material is considered suitable for ad hoc repair and restoration work in existing buildings and monuments.

blockList.listIntroduction: 2 On receipt of a justified request and with the agreement of the FOPH, the FOEN may grant exemptions to the prohibition specified in Number 2 letter b for appliances and equipment with asbestos-containing components if they:

item.p: were in operation before 1 March 1990; and
only contain small quantities of asbestos, solely in a bound form.

content.p: 4 The prohibition specified in Number 2 letter d does not apply to the use of asbestos-containing preparations and articles for a purpose for which placing on the market under paragraph 1 or 2 has been authorised.

blockList.listIntroduction: 1 The manufacturer may only place asbestos on the market if the packaging is marked with:

item.p: the name of the manufacturer;
a warning about the dangers of asbestos to human health and the environment and reference to protective measures; it must comply with the following specifications:

td.p: black or white text on red background

content.p: 2 The manufacturer must also label asbestos-containing preparations and articles with the markings specified in paragraph 1. If the markings are printed directly on the preparation or article, a single colour contrasting clearly with the background is sufficient for the head and field. In this case, the text fields may also be combined under a single head, arranged either horizontally or vertically.
3 In articles with asbestos-containing components, the manufacturer must clearly label these components must be clearly labelled with the markings specified in paragraph 1.

4 If, for important reasons, a preparation or article cannot be marked in accordance with the provisions specified in paragraphs 1–3, the FOEN may, on receipt of a justified request and with the agreement of the FOPH, grant a temporary exemption. It shall require the necessary information to be conveyed to the purchaser in an equivalent form.

blockList.listIntroduction: If asbestos-containing preparations or articles have the potential to release fine dust during use, the manufacturer must provide the user with the following information in writing:

item.p: a warning that inappropriate use poses a risk of lung disease and an increased risk of cancer; and
recommendations on the necessary protective measures.

content.p: 1 The prohibition specified in Number 2 letter d does not apply to uses of asbestos-containing preparations and articles that began before 1 June 2019.
2 Until 30 June 2025, the prohibition specified in Number 2 letter a does not apply to the use of asbestos for the manufacture of diaphragms for existing electrolysis installations.
3 Until 30 June 2025, the prohibitions specified in Number 2 letters b, c and d do not apply to asbestos-containing diaphragms for use in existing electrolysis installations.

FRBRname.value: Ordonnance du 18 mai 2005 sur la réduction des risques liés à l'utilisation de substances, de préparations et d'objets particulièrement dangereux (Ordonnance sur la réduction des risques liés aux produits chimiques, ORRChim)
Ordinance of 18 May 2005 on the Reduction of Risks relating to the Use of Certain Particularly Dangerous Substances, Preparations and Articles (Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance, ORRChem)

Ordinanza del 18 maggio 2005 concernente la riduzione dei rischi nell'utilizzazione di determinate sostanze, preparati e oggetti particolarmente pericolosi (Ordinanza sulla riduzione dei rischi inerenti ai prodotti chimici, ORRPChim)
Verordnung vom 18. Mai 2005 zur Reduktion von Risiken beim Umgang mit bestimmten besonders gefährlichen Stoffen, Zubereitungen und Gegenständen (Chemikalien-Risikoreduktions-Verordnung, ChemRRV)
